cards.text: Friend, the people of Israel brought so much for the tabernacle that Moses, their leader, had to tell them to stop (Exodus 36:5-7). Now the skilled craftsmen get to work, starting with ten curtains of finely spun linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn, with cherubim skillfully worked into them. Every curtain is the same size.

The ten curtains get joined into two sets of five, with fifty loops of blue material along the edge of each set, lined up across from each other. FIFTY loops, all lined up, and I can't line up twelve cookies on a tray without one rolling off to start a new life.

cards.question: To link the loops on the two sets of linen curtains, the craftsmen make fifty gold clasps. What do the clasps do for the tabernacle?

cards.text: Then come eleven curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle, joined with fifty clasps, and this time the clasps are bronze, not gold. Over the tent go two more coverings: ram skins dyed red, and over that, fine leather. Linen, goat hair, ram skins, leather. Nobody is getting rained on in THAT tent.

Then come the walls: upright frames of acacia wood, twenty on the south side, twenty on the north and more across the back, each one standing on two bases. Crossbars run along the frames, with a central crossbar running through the center from one end to the other.

cards.question: The tabernacle's frames are overlaid with gold, and gold rings are made to hold the ___.

cards.text: Next comes the veil, made from the same blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen as the ten curtains, with cherubim worked into it too, hung on four gold-covered posts with gold hooks. Then comes an embroidered curtain for the entrance to the tent, on five posts with bronze bases. This crew has gone through more yarn than a craft store on clearance day.
Now Bezalel, the craftsman the LORD called by name (Exodus 35:30), builds the ark out of acacia wood. He overlays it with pure gold, inside and out.

cards.question: Bezalel casts four gold rings for the ark's four feet and makes poles overlaid with gold. What are the poles for?

cards.text: Then he makes the mercy seat out of pure gold, with a cherub of hammered gold at each end, all made from one piece of gold. Their wings spread upward, overshadowing the mercy seat, and they face each other, looking toward it.
Next he makes a table of acacia wood, overlaid with pure gold. It gets gold rings and gold-covered poles for carrying it too, which is more travel than I got in YEARS at the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Bezalel makes the gold table's plates, dishes, bowls and pitchers out of pure gold. What are the bowls and pitchers for?

cards.text: Then he hammers out the lampstand from pure gold, all of one piece, with six branches and cups shaped like almond blossoms, and makes its seven lamps of pure gold too. The lampstand and all its utensils come from a talent of pure gold. A whole TALENT of gold for one lampstand, friend, and I came home from a closing sale for a QUARTER.
Next comes the altar of incense, a small square of acacia wood overlaid with pure gold, with gold rings and gold-covered poles for carrying it.

cards.question: True or false: besides building the furnishings, Bezalel also makes the sacred anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense.

cards.text: It's the work of a perfumer, friend. This man builds an ark, hammers a lampstand AND mixes incense, and on my best day I stamp a cookie.

Bezalel builds the altar of burnt offering from acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide, with a horn at each corner, overlaid with bronze. This is not the little incense altar, friend, this one is BIG. Its utensils are bronze, a bronze grate goes under its ledge, and it gets rings and poles for carrying it, built with boards so it's hollow.

Next comes the bronze basin and its stand, made from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Mirrors turned into a basin, and I can't walk past a shiny pan without stopping to fix my mustache.

Then he builds the courtyard all around, with curtains of finely spun linen, a hundred cubits on the south and north sides and fifty on the west and east. The posts stand on bronze bases with silver hooks and bands, the entrance gets an embroidered curtain, and every tent peg is bronze.

Then comes the inventory, recorded at Moses' command by the Levites under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest. After all the old receipts I shared that drawer with, these are the first records I've ever been excited about.

cards.question: True or false: Bezalel made everything that the LORD had commanded Moses.

cards.text: With him is Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, designer and embroiderer.

Then come the totals of gold and silver, and the silver comes from half a shekel per person, from everyone twenty or older who was numbered: 603,550 men. I've seen a group chat fall apart trying to split ONE bill four ways.

cards.question: The silver comes in at 100 talents and 1,775 shekels. What are the hundred talents of silver used for?

cards.text: The 1,775 shekels of silver become hooks, tops and bands for the posts, and the bronze goes into the entrance bases, the bronze altar and its grating, the courtyard bases and every tent peg. Keep that apron on, friend, because the tabernacle story still has more coming.
